facts.text: Dad told me the family secret on my twenty-first. I've used it twice tonight already, just to get the dinner chat right.
facts.why: Dad does tell Tim the secret just after his twenty-first. But Tim doesn't redo the dinner in the dark to get the chat right, so the second line is made up.
facts.fix: Dad told me the family secret on my twenty-first. These days I try to live each day once, but properly.

fix_note.text: Dad told me the family secret on my twenty-first. These days I try to live each day once, but properly.

facts.text: Kit Kat's wedding in the pouring rain
facts.why: The wedding in the downpour is Tim and Mary's. Kit Kat's wedding isn't in the plot; she settles down with Tim's friend Jay.
facts.fix: Tim and Mary's wedding in the pouring rain

facts.text: For the beach walk Dad asks to relive.
facts.why: Tim and his father do go back to a childhood day on the beach near the end. The pages read don't say which of them asks.
facts.fix: For the beach day Tim and Dad go back to.

vibe.verdict: A warm Cornish kiosk that fits the film and uses its big scenes, with one made-up note and the rainy wedding put on the wrong person.
missing: Mary's Kate Moss obsession, and Tim visiting the exhibition until he finds her
'Live each day twice' (Dad's advice before he dies)
How time travel works: a dark cupboard, fists clenched (Dad's first lesson)
Dad's speech about loving three men, including B.B. King and Uncle Desmond (the wedding speech)
Harry's opening night going wrong, and Tim going back to fix it
The wedding in the downpour (Tim and Mary)
ideas: Swap 'Cold Cornish cider' for 'Mary's Kate Moss spritz', after the exhibition Tim visits every day to find her.
Swap the 'Gentle swell easing towards evening' surf line for Dad's 'live each day twice'.
Swap the 'Cornish beef and swede pasties' note for 'One for the first time through, one for the second' (the two-day rule).
Swap 'Dad's ping pong Earl Grey iced tea' for 'Dad's table tennis tea', as the eulogy says he played table tennis with Tim.
